product: MiniMax Speech / T2A v2 (speech-2.8-hd, speech-2.8-turbo, speech-2.6, speech-02, speech-01 families)

sources.title: Text to Speech (T2A) HTTP — MiniMax API Docs
sources.what_it_established: The verbatim language_boost enum (41 values plus auto, Welsh absent); the full live model list speech-2.8-hd/turbo, 2.6-hd/turbo, 02-hd/turbo, 01-hd/turbo; voice_setting parameters speed 0.5-2, vol 0-10, pitch -12..+12 and nine emotions; a pronunciation dictionary exists; NO seed and NO temperature parameter; rate-limit error codes 1002 and 1039 (TPM) exist but thresholds are not published.

sources.title: Voice Clone — MiniMax API Docs
sources.what_it_established: Source audio minimum 10 seconds, maximum 5 minutes, mp3/m4a/wav, up to 20 MB; optional example audio under 8 seconds. NO consent requirement, NO verification, NO statement about the right to clone another person's voice appears in the documentation.

sources.title: MiniMax Speech 2.5 launch announcement
sources.what_it_established: Claims 40+ languages and names the additions (Bulgarian, Danish, Greek, Swedish, Filipino, Hungarian, Spanish, Finnish, Norwegian, Slovak, Swahili, Catalan, Lithuanian, Afrikaans). Welsh is not mentioned. Claims cross-lingual cloning preserves speaker identity and accent across languages — a marketing claim, not a spec.

sources.title: MiniMax subscription pricing
sources.what_it_established: Five tiers from Starter $5/mo to Business $999/mo, 100,000 to 20,000,000 monthly audio points, 10 to 800 voice slots, RPM 10 to 800. Per-character rates and voice-cloning cost are NOT published on this page.

welsh.evidence: language_boost is a closed enum and its 41 values are, verbatim: Chinese, Chinese,Yue, English, Arabic, Russian, Spanish, French, Portuguese, German, Turkish, Dutch, Ukrainian, Vietnamese, Indonesian, Japanese, Italian, Korean, Thai, Polish, Romanian, Greek, Czech, Finnish, Hindi, Bulgarian, Danish, Hebrew, Malay, Persian, Slovak, Swedish, Croatian, Filipino, Hungarian, Norwegian, Slovenian, Catalan, Nynorsk, Tamil, Afrikaans, plus auto. No Welsh. The Speech 2.5 launch post enumerates the newly added languages and Welsh is not among them either.
welsh.rationale: Absent from a closed enum, so MiniMax is DEAD as a stock-Welsh provider — the same position as Cartesia. It stays CONDITIONAL on the same single empirical question, with one wrinkle in its favour and one against. In its favour: language_boost accepts 'auto', so unlike a hard language field there is a documented way to submit text without asserting a language, which is exactly the shape of request a Welsh probe would need; and MiniMax's own cross-lingual cloning claim is the most aggressive of the four ('cross-lingual cloning is no longer a challenge'), which is precisely the property that would carry Aran's north-Welsh or Catrin's south-Welsh into an unlisted language. Against: that claim is a launch-post assertion with no benchmark behind it, and 'auto' language detection on a language the model was never trained on will most likely fall back to English or Irish-adjacent phonetics and produce Welsh with an English mouth. The dialect question is the same as everywhere: no vendor addresses north versus south Welsh, so the only route is that a clone carries its speaker's own dialect. Settle it in phase 2 with a paid probe: clone Aran from 10s-5min of audio, render 20 Welsh course seeds with language_boost auto, have a Welsh speaker score them. Note this is the candidate where the probe is cheapest per attempt and the consent story is weakest.

version_pinning: De facto rather than by policy, and that distinction matters. Eight model ids are simultaneously live — speech-2.8-hd, speech-2.8-turbo, speech-2.6-hd, speech-2.6-turbo, speech-02-hd, speech-02-turbo, speech-01-hd, speech-01-turbo — and model is an explicit request parameter, so you can name an old generation and keep naming it. speech-01 still being callable while 2.8 ships is real evidence of long model lifetimes, and it is the best empirical signal any of the four gives. But there are no DATED snapshots, so 'speech-2.8-hd' is a floating name that MiniMax can retrain underneath us without changing the identifier, and no announcement would be required. No deprecation policy, no notice period and no output-stability guarantee were found anywhere in the documentation. In short: probably stable, provably nothing. For a system whose whole requirement is that a re-render next year sounds like the same person, 'probably' is the wrong word, and this is the axis on which MiniMax is weakest relative to Cartesia and OpenAI.
cloning_consent: MiniMax publishes NO consent requirement, NO verification step and NO statement about the right to clone another person's voice in its voice-cloning documentation. That is not a neutral finding — of the four candidates it is the only one where I could not locate any consent obligation at all, and Tom should read that as a risk rather than as convenience. What it needs technically: 10 seconds to 5 minutes of source audio, mp3/m4a/wav, up to 20 MB, optionally an example clip under 8 seconds. WHAT TO SAY TO ARAN AND CATRIN: MiniMax will not ask them for anything. There is no form, no consent recording, no identity check — we upload audio and a voice exists. So the consent record is entirely ours to create and keep, and they should be told that their voice would be uploaded to a Chinese-platform API whose terms on training-data reuse and voice deletion I could not verify from the documentation. Given this project exists because Tom will not feed Aran's voice to a company he does not want it in, that unverified position is a substantive objection, not a paperwork gap.

controls.seed: Absent. No seed parameter in the T2A API.
controls.other: voice_setting exposes speed (0.5-2), vol (0-10), pitch (-12 to +12) and nine named emotions including happy, sad, angry and whisper. A pronunciation dictionary for custom pronunciation rules is documented, which puts MiniMax ahead of Chatterbox and level with Cartesia on the ability to force a word. language_boost accepts an explicit language or 'auto'.

self_host: No. Hosted API only; no weights, no on-prem offer in the public documentation.
pricing: NOT VERIFIED FROM VENDOR DOCUMENTATION — flagged rather than asserted. The official pricing page publishes subscription tiers (Starter $5/mo to Business $999/mo, 100,000 to 20,000,000 monthly audio points, 10 to 800 voice slots) but no per-character rate and no voice-cloning cost. Third-party sources consistently report roughly $100 per million characters for HD models and $60 per million for Turbo, and roughly $0.50-$1.50 per clone via resellers, but these are not vendor documentation and are recorded here only as an order of magnitude to be confirmed. If those figures hold, MiniMax HD is around three times the price of Cartesia per character.
rate_limits: RPM by tier, from 10 (Starter) to 800 (Business). The API defines rate-limit error code 1002 and a separate TPM-exceeded code 1039, so a token-per-minute ceiling exists, but its value is not published. 10 RPM on the entry tier is far too low for bulk course rendering; the tier would have to be sized to the job.
gaps: No MiniMax API key on this box. Nothing was measured; every figure is documentation or, for pricing, third-party report.
Per-character pricing and per-clone cost are NOT on any vendor documentation page I could reach. The numbers in circulation are third-party and are labelled as such.
TPM thresholds are undocumented — only the error code exists. Cannot size a bulk re-render from published information.

No consent, verification or voice-ownership terms in the cloning docs at all. Whether uploaded voice audio is reused for training is unverified, which for this project specifically is a material unknown rather than a formality.
No dated model snapshots and no published deprecation policy — model ids are floating names that can be retrained underneath us silently.
Documentation is split across minimax.io and minimaxi.com with several published URLs returning 404; the pages that did resolve are the ones cited.
